## Plan identity and sign-in | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/18466091-plan-identity-and-sign-in
Path: 21-Account-Support/plan-identity-and-sign-in.md

# Plan identity and sign-in


A Claude Desktop on 3P deployment has several separate sign-ins, and most can use a different identity system. List them before you schedule your move. If you're also changing identity providers (IdPs), the order of the two projects matters, because by default claude.ai accepts one IdP at a time.

This guide is for admins of organizations on Claude Enterprise plans.

This article is part of **[Move from Claude Enterprise to Claude Desktop on a cloud provider](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/18426225)**, which defines the terms wave, overlap period, and cutoff date.

## Sign-ins your users will see

[TABLE]

## Connect your IdP to your cloud provider

Each provider's setup guide explains how to connect your IdP.

- **Amazon Bedrock:** Make your IdP **[the identity source for IAM Identity Center](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/bedrock)**. AWS allows **[only one identity source per organization in AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/manage-your-identity-source.html)**. Before you change it, read AWS's **[considerations for changing your identity source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/manage-your-identity-source-considerations.html)**.

- **Google Cloud:** Use **[Workforce Identity Federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)** with **[an OIDC provider in the pool](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/vertex)**. A pool can federate one or more IdPs.

- **Microsoft Foundry:** Foundry uses **[Entra ID directly](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/foundry)**. If you have Conditional Access rules, see **[Sign in through the OS identity broker](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/entra-broker)**.

- **LLM gateway:** Users sign in to **[your IdP](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/gateway)**, and your gateway checks each user's token.

## If you're changing IdPs

- **By default, claude.ai takes one IdP.** **[Each parent organization links to one IdP](important-considerations-before-enabling-single-sign-on-sso-and-jit-scim-provisioning.md)**, and **[all verified domains must use it](set-up-single-sign-on-sso.md)**. The exception is a beta: parent organizations enrolled in centralized management can **[connect more than one IdP](../15-Claude-AI-Features/set-up-multiple-identity-providers-and-split-domains.md)**. A domain can't get a second IdP while any organization uses JIT provisioning, or while Microsoft Login is turned on for that domain. Outside the beta, you can't run the old and new IdPs side by side there.

- **Follow our steps for switching IdPs.** See **[Switching to a different Identity Provider (IdP)](../15-Claude-AI-Features/switching-to-a-different-identity-provider-idp.md)**. Resetting the SSO connection signs out all users. They can sign in by email link until the new connection is live. For Entra ID, see **[Microsoft Entra ID SSO setup](../13-Enterprise-Admin/microsoft-entra-id-sso-setup.md)**.

- **Make sure email addresses match exactly.** Claude **[matches SSO logins to seats by email](../13-Enterprise-Admin/microsoft-entra-id-sso-scim-email-mismatch.md)**. A mismatch in the new IdP **[creates duplicate accounts](../15-Claude-AI-Features/switching-to-a-different-identity-provider-idp.md)**, and a SCIM email change **[removes the old user and creates a new one](../13-Enterprise-Admin/how-scim-sync-works-for-enterprise-organizations.md)**. Fix mismatches before anyone imports.

- **Check whether your Enterprise Admin Console organization shares the connection.** If it **[uses the existing SSO connection, SCIM directory, and verified domains](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/admin-console)**, one IdP serves both. Before you reset SSO or close the older organization, ask your Anthropic account team how it affects the Enterprise Admin Console organization and the devices it manages.

We recommend this order:

1.  Connect the new IdP to your cloud provider first, and pilot sign-in there. On AWS, if IAM Identity Center already uses the old IdP, this step replaces that organization's one identity source. You can't pilot the two side by side in the same AWS organization.

2.  If the old IdP will stay in service long enough, leave the claude.ai SSO connection alone until the last wave has imported.

3.  If the old IdP retires sooner, make the switch between waves. Don't switch while a wave is importing. Compare the email attributes in both IdPs first.

4.  Keep claude.ai sign-in and member data export working until the final import is done.

## Settings for the overlap period

- **Sign-in screen:** Users can choose claude.ai or your provider configuration. **[`deploymentMode`](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/mdm#restrict-a-device-to-one-deployment-mode)** set to `3p` hides the claude.ai option (Claude Desktop 4.16336.0 or later). Set it in a device profile that also sets your connection. For earlier versions, also set `disableDeploymentModeChooser` to `true`. You can't set either key in the console. Don't set them on a device the console manages, because they **[make the app stop using the console](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/admin-console#keep-a-device-on-its-managed-profile)**.

- **Organization lock:** **[`forceLoginOrgUUID`](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/admin-console#keep-a-device-on-its-managed-profile)** limits standard sign-in on the device to your organization. It also accepts **[a list of organization IDs](../13-Enterprise-Admin/enterprise-configuration-for-claude-desktop.md)**. With the console, include your Enterprise Admin Console organization's ID as well as your Claude Enterprise organization's, and update devices to 2.37337.0 or later first. Otherwise, the console's settings don't apply.

- **Network allowlist:** **[Tenant Restrictions](../13-Enterprise-Admin/enforce-network-level-access-control-with-tenant-restrictions.md)** uses a header that lists allowed organization IDs. Make sure it includes every organization your users still sign in to.

- **Users in two organizations:** A console user who also belongs to another organization is **[asked whether to switch, and each switch restarts the app](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/admin-console)**. Turn on **Require this organization in Claude Desktop** so users can't dismiss the prompt. If your Claude Enterprise organization blocks other accounts in Claude Desktop, first add the Enterprise Admin Console organization's ID to its Allowed organizations list.

- **Claude Code CLI:** List both providers in `allowedProviders` during the overlap period. **[`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`](../02-Claude-Code-CLI/authentication.md)** gives each account its own configuration directory.

---

## Public Sector FAQs | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13756069-public-sector-faqs
Path: 21-Account-Support/public-sector-faqs.md

# Public Sector FAQs

March 25, 2026


## 1. Products and features

### What products are available to Public Sector customers?

Select your product based on both your technical/functional requirements, and also your compliance/security/deployment environment requirements. Here is a list of options:


### What is Claude for Government (C4G)?

Claude for Government is Anthropic's FedRAMP-High authorized product, which is available to both government customers and contractors.

Learn more here: **[Offering expanded Claude access across all three branches of the U.S. government](../19-Reference/offering-expanded-claude-access-across-all-three-branches-of-government.md)**

### How do I access Claude for Government?

Submit a request here: **[Contact Sales](https://claude.com/contact-sales)**

### What is the difference between Claude Enterprise and Claude for Government?

Claude Enterprise (CE) has robust enterprise-level security features that meet many standards of highly regulated industry and is appropriate for the majority of State and Local government uses. Claude for Government (C4G) is our standalone application that is FedRAMP-High authorized. C4G does not yet include Claude Code or Cowork (though they are on the roadmap to be released this year).

### Does Claude for Government include Claude Code?

Not yet; though it’s coming this year. Until then, customers can use Claude Code through Bedrock or Vertex if they need a FedRAMP authorized environment.

### Can I use Claude API in government environments?

Yes. Claude API is available via Amazon Bedrock (in AWS GovCloud - FedRAMP High, and in IL5+) and Google Vertex with Assured Workloads (FedRAMP-High).

For more information, see our **[Claude Code product page](../15-Claude-AI-Features/product-claude-code.md)**.

### What models are available in Claude for Government?

Our Claude for Government application is updated with our latest commercial model releases.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. FedRAMP, Impact Levels, and compliance

### What types of data can be used in Claude?

CUl and FIPS 199 High Impact data are authorized in Claude for Government, which is FedRAMP High authorized. Additionally, per our third-party NIST attestation, Claude Enterprise meets compliance requirements for CUl as well. The third-party NIST attestation is available under NDA here: **[\[Anthropic\] 2026 NIST 800-171r3 Attestation Letter](https://trust.anthropic.com/resources?s=zfucqt7j6yandbrsvlk2&name=%5Banthropic%5D-2026-nist-800-171-r-3-attestation-letter)**

ITAR data can only be processed in Claude via AWS Bedrock, which is IL5 accredited.

For most other government agencies like State and Local handling PHI or PII:, Anthropic offers a HIPAA-ready configuration for Enterprise and API customers, including the ability to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). A couple of key points:

- The BAA is available for Enterprise plans and direct API customers—not consumer (Free, Pro, Max) or Team plans.

- It requires a Zero Data Retention (ZDR) agreement, meaning Anthropic does not store your inputs or outputs.

- Certain features/integrations have limitations under the BAA (e.g., web search is excluded).

You can learn more here:

- BAA details: **[Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers](../13-Enterprise-Admin/business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers.md)**

- Certifications overview (HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001): **[What Certifications has Anthropic obtained?](../19-Reference/what-certifications-has-anthropic-obtained.md)**

- **[Trust Portal](https://trust.anthropic.com)**

### What is Claude's FedRAMP authorization level?

Claude for Government (C4G), and Claude via Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud and Google Vertex with Assured Workloads are all FedRAMP-High.

Learn more here: **[Claude in Amazon Bedrock: Approved for use in FedRAMP High and DoD IL4/5 workloads](../19-Reference/claude-in-amazon-bedrock-fedramp-high.md)**

### Are Claude's models themselves FedRAMP authorized?

FedRAMP and DoD Impact Levels are certifications for cloud services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS). AI models are software components, not cloud services. Claude models deploy within authorized environments, and customers maintain their compliance posture through the hosting platform.

### How can I get access to your FedRAMP authorization information and other associated documentation?

Please submit a request for the package directly to FedRAMP using this **[FedRAMP Package Access Request Form](https://www.fedramp.gov/resources/documents/Agency_Package_Request_Form.pdf)**.

### Can I use Claude for CUI (Controlled Unclassified Information)?

Yes. Claude Enterprise has received a third-party NIST attestation for use of CUI data. Alternatively, CUI data can be processed in a FedRAMP High environment via Claude for Government, Bedrock, or Vertex. The third-party NIST attestation is available under NDA here: **[\[Anthropic\] 2026 NIST 800-171r3 Attestation Letter](https://trust.anthropic.com/resources?s=zfucqt7j6yandbrsvlk2&name=%5Banthropic%5D-2026-nist-800-171-r-3-attestation-letter)**

### Can I use Claude in IL6/Secret environments?

Yes. Claude is available in the AWS Secret region (IL6) via Amazon Bedrock.

### If a customer purchases Claude Enterprise via AWS Marketplace, is that FedRAMP?

No. At present, our only product offering on AWS Marketplace is Claude Enterprise which is not FedRAMP authorized. Customers requiring FedRAMP compliance must use Claude for Government (C4G) or access Claude models through FedRAMP-authorized CSPs (Bedrock GovCloud or Vertex Assured Workloads).

Learn more here: **[Claude in Amazon Bedrock: Approved for use in FedRAMP High and DoD IL4/5 workloads](../19-Reference/claude-in-amazon-bedrock-fedramp-high.md)**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Cloud service providers and deployment

### How do I deploy Claude in Amazon Bedrock on AWS GovCloud / GCP Vertex in Assured Workloads?

Work with your AWS / GCP account teams. Claude is available as a managed service through Bedrock/Vertex. These links can help to get you started:

- **[Access Amazon Bedrock foundation models in AWS GovCloud (US)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html#model-access-govcloud)**

- **[Claude on Vertex AI](../04-API-Reference/Guides/build-with-claude-claude-on-vertex-ai.md)**

### What is the pricing and commitment information for Claude on Vertex/Bedrock?

Contact AWS directly for pricing and commitment requirements. Usage is typically pay-per-token through standard Bedrock pricing.

Learn more here: **[Claude in Amazon Bedrock: Approved for use in FedRAMP High and DoD IL4/5 workloads](../19-Reference/claude-in-amazon-bedrock-fedramp-high.md)**

**AWS Bedrock: [Amazon Bedrock pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/)**

**Google Cloud Vertex AI:** **[Cost of building and deploying AI models in Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing)**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Pricing and procurement

### What is the \$1/month government offer and who qualifies?

The \$1/month offer is specifically for federal, judicial, and legislative agencies for C4G only. It does not extend to defense contractors, FFRDCs, or state/local governments, which receive standard pricing.

### Can we purchase directly from Anthropic or only through Carahsoft?

Both options are available. Anthropic can sell directly, and/or resell / distribute via Carahsoft to specific government customers.

### How much does Claude cost?

C4G is \$60/seat/month with usage limits and no additional consumption charges.

Claude Enterprise is \$20/seat/month with additional charges for token consumption (PAYG).

Other pricing plans are available here: **[Team and Enterprise plan pricing](../17-Billing-Plans/pricing.md#team-&-enterprise)**

Learn more here: **[Offering expanded Claude access across all three branches of the U.S. government](../19-Reference/offering-expanded-claude-access-across-all-three-branches-of-government.md)**

## Cyber Verification Program | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude-opus-and-sonnet
Path: 21-Account-Support/real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude-opus-and-sonnet.md

# Cyber Verification Program


This article explains what the Cyber Verification Program (CVP) is, who can join, how to apply, and how to turn on access after you're approved.

The Cyber Verification Program is available on paid Claude plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise), in Claude Console with billing set up, and through linked cloud accounts and third-party platforms. It isn't available on the Free plan.

**Updated October 6, 2026.** The Cyber Verification Program (CVP) previously covered Claude Opus 5, 4.8, and 4.7, and Sonnet 5 with a single level of access. CVP now offers three access tiers for Claude Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet models starting with Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5.

## Program overview

The Cyber Verification Program lets verified security professionals use our most capable models for advanced security work with fewer interruptions from our cyber safeguards.

You don’t need CVP for everyday secure development. You can use our generally available models to review code, patch known issues, and triage security alerts.

You may need CVP if Claude blocks your security work, such as validating exploits or running authorized penetration tests. Organizations can apply for any tier. Individuals, such as independent researchers, open-source maintainers, and bug bounty hunters, can apply for Defense Access.

Every tier includes Claude Mythos, Opus, and Sonnet models starting with Claude Mythos 5.2, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5. CVP adjusts the safeguards on these models based on your tier. Our **[Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup)** still applies in full.

## Access tiers

Below we share an overview of the three access tiers in the Cyber Verification Program: Defense Access, Red Team Access, and Specialized Access.

[TABLE]

We prohibit some activity in every tier, including:

- Mass destruction of data or devices

- Denial-of-service attacks

- Physical-world damage

- Extortion

- Election interference

- Any request with stated malicious intent

Defense Access suits most critical infrastructure operators. Operating critical infrastructure doesn’t by itself qualify organizations for Specialized Access.

**Note:** You may experience some model refusals and classifier blocks for allowed security work as we continue to refine our safeguards and reduce false positives for approved work across tiers.

## Availability

[TABLE]

## Data retention

Data retention is required for everyone enrolled in the program so that we can help monitor and mitigate cyber misuse. If your organization has a data retention exemption for Claude Fable or Claude Mythos models, you can use CVP with zero data retention (ZDR) on all models in the program for internal use.

Once Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) is generally available, eligible organizations can store data in cloud infrastructure they control. **[Register your interest in EFS](https://claude.com/form/enterprise-frontier-safeguards)**.

## Prepare your application

By default, CVP is only allowed for internal use. A separate application is required for external use:

- **Internal use:** Security work on your own organization’s code, products, and infrastructure. This also includes bug bounty research and coordinated disclosure that you do independently, within the program’s rules, rather than for a client. Every approved tier covers this.

- **External use:** Security work for your customers, or a product they use. This needs a separate approval after you join CVP and are approved for internal use.

### Internal use: what to prepare

#### All tiers

- **The right account.** Make sure you're applying from the organization where you'll use CVP. Approval doesn't carry over to your other organizations. Your Claude and Claude Console accounts are separate organizations.

- **Your email address.** If you're applying as an organization, use an account with your organization's email domain, if applicable. You can't change your account's email address later, so be sure to use the correct email when creating an account.

- **One application.** Submit one application per organization. An Owner or Primary Owner for Claude accounts, or an Admin for Claude Console accounts must submit your organization’s application. Other users in your organization shouldn’t apply separately.

- **Verification details.** Have information ready about your organization and the person applying. Learn more about **[identity verification on Claude](identity-verification-on-claude.md)**.

  - If you're verifying as an individual, have these ready:

    - **A valid government-issued photo ID**: the physical document such as a passport, driver's license, state/provincial ID card, or national identity card (not photocopies)

    - **A phone with a camera**: you may be asked to take a live selfie with your phone.

  - If you're verifying on behalf of an organization, you also need:

    - **Identifying information about your organization:** legal name, address, and business registration number

- **Your security work.** Describe what your team does and how you’ll use Claude.

#### Additional items to prepare by tier

**Defense Access**

Ensure your organization can attest it has the following security controls in place: multi-factor authentication (MFA) and API keys replaced at least every seven days.

**Important:** Starting December 15, 2026, Defense Access also requires phishing-resistant MFA and no longer allows static or long-lived API keys. We recommend that you move to **[Workload Identity Federation](../04-API-Reference/Other/manage-claude-workload-identity-federation.md)** now.

You’ll complete identity verification (business verification for organizations), describe your security work, and accept the terms.

**Red Team Access**

Ensure your organization can attest it has the following security controls in place: phishing-resistant MFA, API keys replaced at least every seven days, company-domain accounts, organization-controlled devices, outbound network controls, and background checks.

Then, find the row that describes your situation, and prepare the relevant information. Matching a row doesn’t guarantee approval.

**Note:** If your organization relies on outside testers, the testing firm should apply to the program.

[TABLE]

**Specialized Access**

We review every Specialized Access application in depth in collaboration with the US government. This tier is for organizations specifically focusing on red teaming systemically important infrastructure. Most critical infrastructure organizations working on defense do not need Specialized Access. To qualify, you'll need to show that you're authorized to test these types of systems and detail the activities you can't accomplish in the Red Team Access tier.

If you're applying for Specialized Access, ensure your organization can attest it has the following security controls in place: phishing-resistant MFA, API keys replaced at least every seven days, company-domain accounts, organization-controlled devices, outbound network controls, and background checks, plus single sign-on and managed devices with malware protection.

#### Evidence that speeds up your review

- Link to sources we can check independently, such as a public registry, certification directory, or issuer page. Upload the full, dated document if there’s no public link. A LinkedIn profile or a screenshot usually isn’t enough. Your own website works for some items, such as a public trust center page listing your certificate or a page describing your testing services.

- Make sure the name on your evidence matches the organization or person we’re verifying.

- Check that every link works and is publicly visible, including bug bounty profiles.

### External use: what to prepare

Each service or product you offer needs its own approval. You can apply once your organization is approved for a CVP tier.

[TABLE]

**Important:** Serving customers through a service or product without explicit approval is a violation of the CVP terms and grounds for removal from the program.

## How to apply

Apply in the **[Verification Portal](https://portal.anthropic.com/programs)**. The portal walks you through verification, your tier, any evidence your tier needs, and the program terms.

You'll verify as a business or an individual. Choose carefully, because the type of verification affects your application:

- **Business**: You're applying for a company, nonprofit, university, government team, or other organization. For Red Team or Specialized Access, you must apply from an account on a Team, Enterprise, or API plan.

- **Individual**: You're applying for yourself, such as an independent researcher, open-source maintainer, or bug bounty hunter. Individuals can apply only for Defense Access. You can apply for Defense Access with a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, or API plan.

### Apply with an Anthropic account

If you use Claude, Claude Code, or the Claude API directly through Anthropic, follow these steps:

1.  Sign in to the **[Verification Portal](https://portal.anthropic.com/programs)** with your Anthropic account. If you don't have one yet, create a new one and set up billing.

2.  Choose “Cyber Verification Program” from the list of programs.

3.  Click “Apply” and complete the application.

4.  Accept the terms and submit.

### Apply with a cloud account

If you use Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Platform on Google Cloud, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Amazon Bedrock (if eligible for EFS), or Microsoft Foundry, follow these steps:

1.  Create an Anthropic account if you haven’t already. It’s free and doesn’t require billing information, but you can’t apply until you link a cloud account or buy Claude Console credits.

2.  Sign in to the Verification Portal for **[Claude Platform on AWS](https://portal.anthropic.com/link?account_source=aws&program=cvp)**, **[Claude Platform on Google Cloud](https://portal.anthropic.com/link?account_source=gcp&program=cvp)**, **[Google Cloud Agent Platform](https://portal.anthropic.com/link?account_source=gcp&program=cvp)**, **[Amazon Bedrock](https://portal.anthropic.com/link?account_source=aws&program=cvp)**, or **[Microsoft Foundry](https://portal.anthropic.com/programs)** with your Anthropic account, or sign up if you don't have one.

3.  You'll be prompted to link your Cloud Service Provider account with a CLI command, to verify that you are an admin. You can link up to 10 GCP projects or AWS accounts.

4.  Open **Programs** and choose “Cyber Verification Program” from the list of programs.

5.  Click “Apply” and complete the application.

6.  Accept the terms and submit.

Then, follow these steps with your cloud provider account:

1.  Open **[Linked accounts](https://portal.anthropic.com/linked-accounts)**, select “Link account,” and choose your provider.

2.  Enter your account details and complete the setup step for your provider:

    1.  **AWS:**

        1.  **What to enter:** 12-digit account ID

        2.  **Setup step:** Create the verification role using the portal’s launch link or command. Link Claude Platform on AWS before Bedrock.

    2.  **Google Cloud:**

        1.  **What to enter:** Project ID (not the project number)

        2.  **Setup step:** Run the `gcloud` command shown.

    3.  **Azure:**

        1.  **What to enter:** Subscription ID and directory (tenant) ID

        2.  **Setup step:** Deploy a Claude model in Foundry first, then run the commands shown.

3.  Select “I’ve granted access,” then “Verify.”

4.  Choose “Cyber Verification Program,” and click “Apply" from the Programs page.

### Apply through a third-party platform

1.  Ask your platform for an Anthropic enrollment link.

2.  Open the link, sign in to the Verification Portal or create an account, and confirm that you would like your account linked.

3.  Choose “Cyber Verification Program,” and click “Apply” from the Programs page.

### Apply for external use

You must be an Owner or Primary Owner of a Claude account or an Admin of a Claude Console account that’s approved for CVP. Then you can:

1.  Open **[Cyber productization](https://portal.anthropic.com/programs/cyber-productization)** in the Verification Portal.

2.  Select “Register an offering” and choose your type.

3.  For a managed service, complete the form, accept the Anthropic Cyber Defender Partner Addendum, and select “Submit for Review.” For a product, describe it in one line, add a name and email, and select “Express interest.”

**Note:** You can’t edit or withdraw this application after you submit it. Repeat these steps for each additional service or product.

## What to expect after you apply

### When you’ll hear back

We’ll email you with a decision or a request for more information. To check your status, sign in to the Verification Portal, open Programs, and choose "Cyber Verification Program." If your review takes longer than the target, you don't need to reapply or contact support.

[TABLE]

If you apply for Red Team Access or Specialized Access and qualify for a lower tier, you will receive access to the lower tier while we review the rest of your application.

### If you’re not approved

You can keep using our generally available models, along with any tier you did get approved for.

You also can reapply after seven days**.** This is the best option if something has changed or you can provide stronger evidence to support your application. Check that you’re applying from the right account and completed the right kind of verification, business or individual.

We may review, narrow, or withdraw program access at any time in our sole discretion if we see activity that violates our policies.


## What to do after you’re approved

### 1. Turn on access

**Important:** On most products, approval doesn’t "turn on" CVP. Your admin needs to assign the program to the proper roles and workspaces first.

[TABLE]

#### Claude Console

To turn on access to CVP in Claude Console:

1.  **[Sign in to the Console](../04-API-Reference/Other/playground.md)** as an organization admin. You'll have the option to either create a new **[workspace](../04-API-Reference/Other/playground.md)** or assign CVP access to one you already have. **Note:** You can't assign it to the default workspace.

2.  Add only users that should get access to the advanced cyber capabilities to the workspace. For Red Team Access and Specialized Access, the Console shows how many seats you're using. Every organization admin counts as a seat. If you go over your tier’s limit, every workspace loses CVP access until you’re back within it.

3.  Open the **[Programs page](https://platform.claude.com/settings/programs)** and select the card for your tier, such as “Defense Access.”

4.  In the **Workspaces** table, turn on the **Access** switch for your workspace.

5.  If a cell in the workspace’s row says “Not set,” “Not met,” or “Allowed,” select it and follow the fix. Until December 15, 2026, Defense Access allows only API keys that expire within seven days. After that date, it doesn’t allow API keys. Red Team Access and Specialized Access need API keys turned off.

6.  Check the page’s count of active workspaces, such as “1 of 2 workspaces active.” A workspace stays inactive until it meets the requirements.

For details, see **[assign a program to workspaces](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16764810)**.

#### Claude Enterprise

To turn on access to CVP in Claude Enterprise:

1.  Sign in as an Owner or Primary Owner.

2.  Go to **Organization settings \> Roles** and add or edit a custom role.

3.  Select the **Details** tab, then choose the groups that need access.

4.  Select the **Models** tab, then choose the grant under **Grants** and save.

5.  Confirm that your approved users have the **Custom** role type. Built-in roles aren’t covered.

For details, see **[assign a program to a custom role](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17118092).**

#### Google Cloud Agent Platform

To turn on access to CVP in Google Cloud Agent Platform, repeat these steps for each project:

1.  In the **[Verification Portal](https://portal.anthropic.com/programs)**, go to **[Linked accounts](https://portal.anthropic.com/link?account_source=gcp&program=cvp)** and link your project.

2.  Go to **Programs** and turn on your tier.

3.  In **Model Garden**, open the Claude model and accept the Advanced AI Safety Addendum.

4.  Turn on data sharing for each model and location you use. Set `dataSharingEnabledProvider` to `ANTHROPIC` with Google’s `setPublisherModelConfig` API.

#### Claude Mythos on cloud providers

Access to Mythos on cloud partners starts about five business days after you’re approved for CVP. If you have a committed contract with Anthropic, your account team will send you a short form. Complete it, then accept the private offer in your cloud marketplace. We’ll provision Mythos once both steps are done.

### 2. Give each team the right tier

If you’re approved for more than one tier, treat each grant like any other privileged access. Keep each grant in its own workspace, role, or cloud account.

- **Specialized Access:** The small group whose work is still blocked in Red Team Access

- **Red Team Access:** red teamers, penetration testers, and offensive security researchers

- **Defense Access:** the rest of your security team, plus developers and other employees who do security or security-adjacent work

- **No grant:** everyone else

## Frequently asked questions

### I’m approved. Why am I still blocked?

Ask your admin to confirm they’ve assigned you access. If you use Claude Console, check that you’re in the workspace with the program applied. Then check that the work falls within your tier.

### I have Defense Access. Can I apply for a higher tier?

Yes, if you applied as an organization. You’ll keep Defense Access while we review your application.

### Can different parts of my company have different tiers?

Yes. Each Claude organization needs its own application. Within one organization, you can assign programs by workspace (Console) or role (Enterprise). Team plans can’t split access between users.

### I work at a security firm. Does my tier cover work for clients?

Not by itself. You need a CVP tier and approval for external use, usually as a managed service.

### Can I use CVP internally if another workspace serves customers?

In Claude Console, yes. CVP applies only to the workspaces you assign it to, and it can’t be the Default workspace. Assign it to a workspace used only for internal work, and keep customer traffic in a separate workspace without CVP. To use CVP for customer traffic, you need approval for external use.

On Team plans, access applies to your whole organization, so you can’t limit it to internal work. Don’t serve customers from an organization with CVP access until we’ve approved that service or product for external use.

### Why is access on Amazon Bedrock limited?

Bedrock doesn’t yet support human review of automated safety flags, which CVP requires by default. For now, CVP on Bedrock is available only to organizations with a data retention exemption. Once Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) is available, Bedrock organization in the EFS program can apply for CVP access. To register your interest in EFS, use this **[Enterprise Frontier Safeguards form](https://claude.com/form/enterprise-frontier-safeguards)**. In the interim, we're working to expand CVP to Bedrock customers. Contact your account team to ask about an exemption.

### How do usage limits work for Claude Mythos models?

Mythos models follow the same usage rules as Claude Fable models.

- **Pro plan:** Mythos models are available only with usage credits.

- **Max and Ultra plans:** Mythos and Fable models share up to 50% of your weekly usage limit. This usage also counts toward your regular usage limits. After that, you can continue with usage credits, if they’re turned on, or switch to another model.

### Can I download a copy of my application?

Yes. You can download your application and terms as a PDF from the program page in the Verification Portal.

### Can I add more people after I’m approved?

Yes. You don’t need to reapply. Your admin adds them to the workspace (Console) or custom role (Enterprise) that has the program, up to your tier’s limit. For Red Team Access and Specialized Access, you can add only people on the team named in your application. Everyone you add must meet your tier’s security requirements.

### Can I add another cloud account after I’m approved?

Yes. Link the new account to the same Anthropic organization in the Verification Portal. You don’t need a new application. On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Agent Platform, you also need to turn on your tier for the new account.

### Does CVP change safeguards outside of cybersecurity?

No. CVP adjusts only our cyber safeguards. Our safeguards from other domains like research biology still apply in every tier. Our **[Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup)** still applies in full.

### Can I change or cancel my application after I submit it?

No. You can review and edit your answers until you submit, but you can’t edit or cancel an application after that. If you’re not approved, you can reapply after seven days.

### I was approved on the wrong organization. What should I do?

Apply again from the organization where you’ll use CVP, or ask your account team for help.

---

## Respond to an Enterprise domain claim on your Claude account | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14625626-respond-to-an-enterprise-domain-claim-on-your-claude-account
Path: 21-Account-Support/respond-to-an-enterprise-domain-claim-on-your-claude-account.md

# Respond to an Enterprise domain claim on your Claude account


If your organization has set up Claude Enterprise, they may claim your existing personal Claude account (Free, Pro, Max, or Ultra). This article explains what to expect and what your options are.

**Note:** If your admin hasn't claimed your domain yet and you're exploring your options, see **[Move your personal Claude account to a Team or Enterprise organization](can-individuals-with-pro-or-max-plan-accounts-migrate-them-to-team-or-enterprise-plan.md)**.

## What it means when your domain is claimed

Your organization’s admin has initiated a process called domain claiming. This means all personal Claude accounts tied to your company’s email domain (for example, *@yourcompany.com*) will close. Before a deadline, you choose whether to bring what you can into your organization’s Enterprise workspace.

You’ll receive an email and an in-product notification letting you know that your account has been claimed, along with a deadline to choose what happens to your data. This deadline is at least 30 days from the date your admin initiates the claim.

The notification is a banner at the top of Claude, on the web and in Claude Desktop, titled "Choose what happens to your personal data." Click "See options" to make a choice. The banner appears in your personal account, and in your organization if you’ve already joined.

## Your two options

**Note:** If your organization has turned on HIPAA readiness or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), the **Bring what you can** option isn't available. Your only option is to start fresh. **[Export your data](../22-Safety-Policy/export-your-claude-data.md)** before the deadline if you want a copy. The export doesn’t include the original files you uploaded. Your subscription is still handled as described below. Learn more about **[HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13296973)** and **[customer-managed encryption keys](../22-Safety-Policy/what-are-customer-managed-encryption-keys-cmek-claude-help-center.md)**.

### Bring what you can

Bring your existing data into your organization's Enterprise workspace. Some things don't move. Most importantly, custom skills, Claude Docs, Cowork tasks in the cloud, and your connected apps are left in your personal account. To bring your data, you need a seat in your organization. Ask your admin for one. Before you confirm, you’ll see the list of what will and won’t move from your account. Save what won’t move first (see **[Before you migrate](can-individuals-with-pro-or-max-plan-accounts-migrate-them-to-team-or-enterprise-plan.md#h_c1ec8a383d)**). For the full list of what does and doesn’t move, see **[What moves when you migrate](can-individuals-with-pro-or-max-plan-accounts-migrate-them-to-team-or-enterprise-plan.md#h_4e63ef6e87)**.

After the move, your personal account closes and will be deleted, along with anything that didn’t move, per our data retention practices. **This can’t be undone.** If you subscribed through the Apple App Store, your personal account closes a few weeks after you move, then it's deleted, per our data retention practices. What moved stays in your organization’s workspace. Learn more about **[how long Anthropic stores your data](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data)**.

### Start fresh

Your existing data won’t move to your organization’s Enterprise workspace. Your personal account closes, and its data will be deleted, per our **[data retention practices](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data)**.

If you want a copy, you can get one in two ways:

- Before you choose "Start fresh," sign in to your personal account, go to **[Settings \> Privacy](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls)**, export your data, and download the file.

- After you choose "Start fresh," pick "Download your data." We’ll email you a link after your personal account closes. The link expires after 24 hours and may work only once, so download the file right away. Claude for Teachers and FERPA-covered accounts don’t get a download link. Export and download your data before you choose **Start fresh**. For Claude for Teachers, go to **[Organization settings \> Data and privacy](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/data-privacy-controls)**. For FERPA-covered accounts, go to **[Settings \> Privacy](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls)**. If you can’t export, **[contact Support](../15-Claude-AI-Features/how-to-get-support.md#h_d6fc679aa4)** before you choose **Start fresh**.

Note that exported data can’t be imported into your organization’s workspace, and it’s for your personal records only. Neither copy includes the original files you uploaded.

## What happens if you don’t choose

**If you don’t make a choice before the deadline, your personal account closes and will be deleted, along with its data**, per our **[data retention practices](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023548-how-long-do-you-store-my-data).** You’ll get an email with a link to download your data. The download doesn’t include the original files you uploaded.

Download the file right away: the link expires after 24 hours and may only work only. It opens only when you’re signed in to Claude with the same email address. If it has expired or won’t open, **[contact Support](../15-Claude-AI-Features/how-to-get-support.md#h_d6fc679aa4)** (an Owner of your organization may need to reach out for you). Claude for Teachers and FERPA-covered accounts don’t get a download link. Export and download your data before the deadline.

For Claude for Teachers, go to **[Organization settings \> Data and privacy](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/data-privacy-controls)**. For FERPA-covered accounts, go to **[Settings \> Privacy](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls)**. If you can’t export, **[contact Support](../15-Claude-AI-Features/how-to-get-support.md#h_d6fc679aa4)** before the deadline. To use Claude in your organization, sign in with single sign-on (SSO). If you can't sign in or don’t see your organization after you sign in, ask your admin to add you. The download link won’t open until you can sign in.

Sign in before the deadline to make your choice.

## What happens to your paid subscription

If you bought a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription directly from us, it will be automatically canceled when you choose an option or when the deadline passes. You’ll receive a prorated refund for any unused time. If you subscribed through Google Play, we ask Google Play to cancel your subscription and refund your unused time. Check Google Play, and cancel there if your plan is still active. See **[How do refunds work for migrated accounts?](can-individuals-with-pro-or-max-plan-accounts-migrate-them-to-team-or-enterprise-plan.md#h_c0aa7afb70)**

**Apple App Store subscriptions:** If you purchased your Pro, Max, or Ultra plan through the Apple App Store, we can’t cancel or refund it directly. You’ll need to cancel it yourself through your Apple ID settings:

1.  Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.

2.  Tap your name at the top, then tap "Subscriptions."

3.  Find your Claude subscription and tap "Cancel Subscription."

If you don’t cancel your App Store subscription, Apple will continue to charge you even though your personal account has been closed.

## How to sign in after migration

After migration, you’ll sign in to Claude using your organization’s single sign-on (SSO) provider. Go to claude.ai and sign in with your work email—you’ll be redirected to your company’s login page. When a move finishes or your personal account closes, you’re signed out on all your devices, so you’ll need to sign in again.

**Can’t sign in?** You may not be set up in your company’s identity provider yet. Contact your IT admin for help.

If you chose "Bring what you can," what moved will be waiting in your organization’s workspace.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I undo a move?

No. Moving is permanent. Once your personal account data is transferred to your organization’s workspace, it can’t be moved back to a personal account. Start fresh can’t be undone either.

### Can I keep my personal account and also join the Enterprise workspace?

No. Once your domain is claimed, personal accounts on that domain can’t coexist with the Enterprise workspace. You’ll need to choose "Bring what you can" or "Start fresh."

### What if I use my personal email, not my work email?

Domain claiming only affects accounts tied to your organization’s verified domain (your work email). If you have a separate Claude account on a personal email address (like Gmail or Yahoo), that account isn’t affected.

### Will my organization be able to see my old conversations?

Yes. Your organization can access what moves, the same way it can access the rest of its data. For example, its Primary Owner can export it. Your organization’s data retention policies apply to it too. For more information, see **[Who owns and manages the data of my team?](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9265372-who-owns-and-manages-the-data-of-my-team)**

### What if I’m not in my company’s identity provider?

If you’re not in your organization’s IdP, you won’t be able to sign in to the Enterprise workspace after migration. Contact your IT admin to make sure you’re added before the deadline. Your admin must add you, with a seat, before you can bring your data.

### I have both a personal account and an existing Enterprise account. What happens?

You can choose "Bring what you can." What can move is added to your organization’s workspace. If your personal and organization settings conflict, your organization’s settings apply.

---

## Set up single sign-on (SSO) | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-set-up-single-sign-on-sso
Path: 21-Account-Support/set-up-single-sign-on-sso.md

# Set up single sign-on (SSO)

October 13, 2026


Single sign-on is available for Team plans, Enterprise plans, and Console organizations.

This guide covers the steps to configure SSO for Team and Enterprise plans, and Claude Console organizations.

## Step 1: Review prerequisites and important considerations

Before proceeding with SSO setup, complete the following:

**Review the considerations guide:** Read **[Important considerations before enabling single sign-on (SSO) and JIT/SCIM provisioning](important-considerations-before-enabling-single-sign-on-sso-and-jit-scim-provisioning.md)** to understand parent organizations, determine your setup path, and complete any prerequisite steps such as merging organizations.

**Confirm you have the required role:**

- For Team or Enterprise plans: You must be an Owner or Primary Owner

- For Claude Console: You must be an Admin

**Confirm you have access to the following:**

- DNS settings for your company's email address domain

- Your company's SSO Identity Provider (IdP) used to log in to third-party applications (e.g., Okta, Google Workspace, etc.)

Please contact your organization's IT Administrator if you do not have permissions to manage Claude or company DNS settings.

**Note:** WorkOS is Anthropic's provider for domain verification and SSO setup. More details can be found in **[Anthropic's Subprocessor List](https://trust.anthropic.com/subprocessors)**. You will be taken through a WorkOS setup flow when configuring SSO and provisioning features—find your Identity Provider in their **[Integration documentation](https://workos.com/docs/integrations)**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 2: Verify your domain(s)

Domain verification proves that you own your company's domain. Once verified, you can configure SSO for accounts with your company's domain.

You can verify multiple domains for a single organization, but all domains must be managed through a single IdP. We don't support verifying domains from separate IdPs within the same organization.

**Note:** Verifying your domain by itself will not impact existing users' ability to access our products. End users’ access is only affected once SSO is set up and explicitly enforced.

1.  Navigate to your **Organization and access** settings in Claude (**[claude.ai/admin-settings/organization](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/organization)**) or your **Identity and access** settings in Console (**[platform.claude.com/settings/identity](https://platform.claude.com/settings/identity)**) – note this page will only appear on Console if you've worked with Sales to enable SSO or completed a merge proposal.

2.  In the **Domains** section, click “Add or edit domains.”

3.  Enter the domain(s) you want to verify in the **Update organization email domains** modal and click the “+” button:


4.  Click “Save” when you’re finished adding domains.

5.  The domain(s) you added will now appear in the **Domains** section; click “Verify” to the right of the domain(s) to begin the verification process.

6.  Enter your domain in the text box and click “Continue”:


7.  The setup screen displays a TXT record. **Copy the full Value using the copy button**—it begins with `anthropic-domain-verification-` and is longer than what's visible in the box. In your DNS provider, add a TXT record to your domain and **Value** set to the copied string. The domain must match exactly what you entered in the previous step, including any subdomains. Add it alongside any existing TXT records; don't replace them. The value is case-sensitive, so paste it exactly. Please refer to your DNS provider's documentation on this topic.

    1.  **Important:** Save the TXT value before leaving the setup screen. Once the domain shows as Pending, the admin console doesn't display the value again. If you lose it, you'll need to remove and re-add the domain, which generates a new value.

8.  Wait 10 minutes for your DNS change to propagate.

    - **Note:** *DNS changes can take 24-48 hours to propagate globally.*

9.  When you see the green "Verified" badge, you can close the instructions page.

10. If your domain shows as "Pending," use the "Refresh" button.

### If your domain stays Pending

Clicking "Refresh" re-checks your DNS; it won't show Verified until the published TXT record exactly matches the expected value. If it stays Pending after DNS has propagated, check the following:

- **The record exists at the root.** Look up your domain's TXT records with a tool such as **[DNSChecker](https://dnschecker.org/#TXT)** and confirm a record beginning with `anthropic-domain-verification-` appears for `yourdomain.com` (not `www.yourdomain.com` or another subdomain). If it doesn't appear, the record may have been added at the wrong host or hasn't propagated yet.

- **The value matches exactly.** The check is case-sensitive and requires the full string including the `anthropic-domain-verification-…=` prefix. A single character difference will keep it Pending.

- **You haven't removed and re-added the domain.** Each re-add generates a new verification value. If you re-added the domain after publishing the TXT record, the published value no longer matches—you'll need to update the DNS record with the new value.

If the record is correct and propagated but the status still shows Pending, contact Support.


**Note:** Once your domain is verified, you'll see a **Restrict organization creation** toggle under **Security** on the Organization and access organization settings page. Enable this if you want to prevent users from creating new Claude or Console organizations—including personal accounts—using your verified domains.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 3: Set up SSO with your Identity Provider

1.  Navigate to your **Organization and access** settings in Claude (**[claude.ai/admin-settings/organization](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/organization)**) or your **Identity and access** settings in Console (**[platform.claude.com/settings/identity](https://platform.claude.com/settings/identity)**).

2.  In the **Authentication** section, click “Setup SSO” (or “Manage SSO”).

3.  Follow the setup guide provided for your Identity Provider (see below for additional guides).

4.  At the end of these steps, you’ll be prompted to Test Single Sign-on to confirm there are no errors and the configuration is successful.

5.  Once complete, navigate back to the **Organization and access** settings page for further configuration options.

**Important:** SSO enforcement might result in users being unable to log in if they are not correctly assigned to the Anthropic app in the IdP. If you have more than one Claude/Console org connected to your “parent org,” you will want to consider creating a unique IdP Group for each. For more information, see **[enable group mappings](../13-Enterprise-Admin/setting-up-jit-or-scim-provisioning.md#h_adee31eeba)**.

For IdP-specific setup instructions, see:

- **[Okta SAML](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/okta-saml)**

- **[Entra ID SAML (formerly Azure AD)](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/entra-id-saml)**

- **[Google SAML](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/google-saml)**

- **[OneLogin SAML](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/onelogin-saml)**

- **[JumpCloud SAML](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/jumpcloud-saml)**

- **[Duo SAML](https://workos.com/docs/integrations/duo-saml/4-enter-duo-saml-settings-in-your-workos-dashboard)**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 4: Choose to require SSO

You can now choose to toggle on **Require SSO for Console** and/or **Require SSO for Claude,** on the **Organization and access** page, under the **Authentication** section:


When SSO is required, users must use the “Continue with SSO” option to log in to their Claude/Console accounts. When SSO is not required, they will have the option to choose “Continue with SSO” or “Continue with email.”

Before you decide, review **[What happens to existing users when SSO is enabled](important-considerations-before-enabling-single-sign-on-sso-and-jit-scim-provisioning.md#h_644f467167)**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Step 5: Choose your provisioning approach

Once SSO is enabled, you need to decide how users will be added to your organization by choosing an option within the **User provisioning** section of your **Organization and access** settings.

**Invite only** is the default. Users are added and removed directly in your Claude or Console settings. Please see **[Manage members on Team and Enterprise plans](../17-Billing-Plans/managing-members-on-team-and-enterprise-plans.md)**.

**Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning** can be enabled to automatically provision users when they first log in. By default, users assigned to your Anthropic IdP app first login, they will receive the User role. This is the simplest automated option and requires no additional configuration beyond selecting "Just-in-Time (JIT)" as your provisioning mode.

### Enable group mappings - when to configure additional provisioning features

For more control over provisioning, see **[Set up JIT or SCIM provisioning](../13-Enterprise-Admin/setting-up-jit-or-scim-provisioning.md)**. You'll want to review this guide if you need to:

- Automatically assign roles or seat tiers based on IdP group membership.

- Use SCIM directory sync for automatic provisioning and deprovisioning.

- Manage access across multiple organizations (e.g., if you have both a Team/Enterprise organization and a Console organization linked to the same parent and need to control which users are provisioned to each).

**Note:** We don't currently support IdP-initiated login for Claude Console organizations that share SSO settings with a Team or Enterprise plan organization. Users will be redirected to claude.ai with IdP-initiated login. As a workaround, if possible in your IdP, create a bookmark called "Claude Console" that links to platform.claude.com/login?sso=true to redirect users to Console for SP-initiated login.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Update your SSO certificate or client secret

When your Identity Provider’s X.509 signing certificate (SAML) or client secret (OpenID Connect) expires or is rotated, you’ll need to update it in Claude or Console to maintain SSO functionality.

1.  Navigate to your settings:

    - For Team and Enterprise plans: **[claude.ai/admin-settings/organization](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/organization)**

    - For Claude Console: **[platform.claude.com/settings/identity](https://platform.claude.com/settings/identity)**

2.  In the **Authentication** section, click “Manage SSO.”

3.  Update the credential for your connection type:

    1.  **SAML:** Find the **Metadata configuration** section, click “Edit,” and update your certificate information.

    2.  **OpenID Connect:** Replace the expired client secret with the new one from your Identity Provider. OpenID Connect connections don’t use a certificate.

4.  Save your changes.

5.  Click "Test sign-in" on the same page to confirm everything is working.

**Important:** If **Require SSO** is turned on and your certificate or client secret has already expired, no one in your organization can sign in to update it, because every sign-in option routes through SSO. **[Contact Support](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9015913)** from an Owner’s or Primary Owner’s email address and we’ll help you regain access so an Owner can update it. To avoid this, note the expiry date of your certificate or client secret in your Identity Provider and rotate it ahead of time.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Turn off SSO

You can toggle **Require SSO for Claude** or **Require SSO for Console** off at any time. This will make SSO optional for all users.

To fully disconnect SSO, click “Manage SSO” then “Reset connection.” This will end all users’ sessions and require them to sign back in via email login link.

## Locked out of admin access?

If none of your Owners or Admins can sign in (for example, after a certificate or client secret expiry, an Identity Provider change, or a group mapping that removed your administrators), contact Support from an Owner’s or Primary Owner’s email address. We’ll verify your ownership of the organization and help you regain access so you can correct the configuration.

---

## Set up your design system in Claude Design | Claude Help Center

Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604397
Path: 21-Account-Support/set-up-your-design-system-in-claude-design-claude-help-center.md

# Set up your design system in Claude Design


A design system captures your colors, typography, components, and layout patterns, so Claude applies them to every new design and deck. Claude extracts them from the assets you provide, like codebases, slide decks, or other design references.

Design systems are available in beta on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans. They're on by default on Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team plans. On Enterprise plans, they're off until an owner turns on **Design systems** in **[Organization settings \> Artifacts](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/artifacts)**. Standalone Claude Design at claude.ai/design has its own separate setting.

This guide is for the designer or brand owner who will set up the design system. On Team and Enterprise plans, you only need to do this once, and everyone's work picks it up after that.

## Before you start

- On Team and Enterprise plans, **Design systems** needs to be on for your organization, and an owner may limit who can publish or set the default.

- You’ll need at least one of the following as source material:

  - A codebase with your design system or component library

  - A slide deck or document that reflects your visual identity

  - Brand guideline assets (logos, color palettes, typography specs)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Create a design system

### From a chat

Ask Claude to build a design system from your connected apps, uploaded files, Figma files, decks, logos, and fonts. This works best for brand design systems with fonts, colors, and guidelines.

### From Claude Code

If your design system already exists as React components, run /design-sync in Claude Code. It reads your tokens and components directly, and works best for product design systems in code.

### Bring over a design system from claude.ai/design

1.  Open the "Design" tab at the bottom of the sidebar.

2.  Click "Move team design systems" in the banner.

Each design system becomes an artifact Claude can use in any chat, including in Claude Code. Design systems may need some cleanup after you move them, so each one shows a banner where you can click "Let Claude clean it up," and Claude tidies its guide, tokens, and components. If your organization has a retention period that covers artifacts, a design system you moved can be permanently deleted if nobody opens it for that period. Opening a design or deck that uses the design system doesn't count as opening it.

## Manage your design systems

Manage your design systems in Settings \> Capabilities by selecting Manage next to Design systems. If Design systems isn't there, go to Settings \> Design systems. On Enterprise plans, admins can reserve publishing, setting the organization default, and deleting design systems for specific users. Learn more in the **[Artifacts admin guide for Team and Enterprise plans](../17-Billing-Plans/artifacts-admin-guide-for-team-and-enterprise-plans-claude-help-center.md)**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Use a design system with a keyboard

To get into and out of the artifact panel, see **[Use artifacts with a keyboard or screen reader](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17457950)**. That article also explains what focus means, what to do on a Mac laptop or in Safari, and how shortcuts are written.

A design system opens as a list of sections beside the section you're reading. Return on a section in the list moves into it, Cmd+F6 (Ctrl+F6 on Windows) moves between the list and the section, and Cmd+Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows) undoes a change when you're not in a text box.

**Note:** Live component previews in a design system can't be reached with Tab, so they can't be operated from the keyboard. Each component's name and notes can be read.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Set up a design system at claude.ai/design

These steps use standalone Claude Design.

### Create or switch to your organization

1.  Open **[Claude Design](https://claude.ai/design)**.

2.  In the lower left corner of the project picker, click the current organization name.

3.  Select your organization, or create a new one.

4.  Complete the onboarding flow you're redirected to.

### Upload your brand and product assets

During onboarding, or afterward from your organization settings, upload the assets that define your brand and product. Claude analyzes them and extracts a reusable design system.

- **Codebases:** If your design system lives in code, like a React component library, link or upload the repository. Claude reads the components and styles.

- **Prototypes:** Screenshots, web flows, and existing design files.

- **Slide decks or documents:** Even a well-designed PowerPoint or PDF that reflects your brand can work. Claude extracts colors, layout patterns, and typographic choices.

- **Individual assets:** Logos, color palette files, typography specimens.

You only need one source to get started, but more sources give Claude more to work with.

### Review the generated design system

After uploading, Claude generates a design system for your organization. This typically includes:

- **Color palette:** Primary, secondary, and accent colors extracted from your assets.

- **Typography:** Font families, sizes, and weights.

- **Components:** Buttons, cards, navigation elements, and other reusable UI patterns.

- **Layout patterns:** Spacing, grid systems, and page structures.

To validate it, create a test project and check whether the output matches your brand. Try prompts like:

- "Create a landing page for \[your product\]."

- "Design a dashboard showing \[relevant metrics\]."

- "Make a one-pager about \[a topic your team commonly presents on\]."

### Make it available to your team

When you're happy with the design system, turn on the "Published" toggle. After publishing, projects created from the Claude Design home screen in your organization use your design system instead of the default.

## Update your design system

When your design system changes, you can update it within Claude Design. From your Claude Design organization settings, click the “Open” button next to the design system you want to edit. Click the “Remix” button in the upper right corner to open the chat interface on the left side of the window. From here, you can work with Claude to change your design system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Tips for best results

- **Include real examples, not just specs.** A finished landing page or marketing site tells Claude more about your brand’s feel than a color palette alone.

- **Iterate.** If the first extraction doesn’t capture your brand well, try uploading additional or different assets.
